title: Validate Binary Tree Nodes
summary: Determine if the nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 can form exactly one valid binary tree, given their left and right children.
statement: Determine if the nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 can form exactly one valid binary tree, given their left and right children. If a node does not have a left child, its leftChild value is -1, and similarly, if it does not have a right child, its rightChild value is -1. Return true if the nodes form a single valid binary tree, otherwise return false.
constraints: Each child entry is -1 or a node index.
All n nodes must form exactly one rooted binary tree.
hints: A tree has one root of indegree zero and every other node indegree one.
Reject multiple parents, then identify the unique root.
Traverse from the root, rejecting revisits, and require exactly n visited nodes.
These checks enforce unique parenthood, acyclicity, and connectedness—the defining tree properties.
editorial: These checks enforce unique parenthood, acyclicity, and connectedness—the defining tree properties.

tests.explanation: Node zero is the unique root and reaches every node exactly once.
Node three has two parents, so the structure is invalid.
